result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers give pasteable, rem-based, mobile and desktop CSS with good body sizes and h1 scaling. A caps the reading column at 65ch and puts the whole scale in custom properties. B sets no max-width at all, and its h3 line-height of 1.4 is looser than the heading range. B's code-to-body ratio is a little better, but leaving out the column cap is the bigger miss. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): B caps prose at 65ch, keeps all heading line-heights in the 1.15-1.25 range, and puts the full size scale in custom properties that a media query overrides, so it's easier to hand off. A has good sizes and a sensible mobile-first structure, but it never limits the article column width. Its h3 line-height of 1.4 is also a little loose for a heading.
